audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Joshua / Yehoshua unconquered-territory and east-Jordan allotment register, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Joshua's old age, remaining land, Philistine and Sidonian territories, promise of future dispossession, nine-and-half-tribe allocation, Reuben/Gad/half-Manasseh boundaries, Balaam death notice, non-dispossessed Geshurites/Maacathites, and Levite inheritance theology.

verses.restored: Joshua was old, advanced in days, and YHWH said to him, You are old, advanced in days, and very much land remains to possess.

familiar.text: Now Joshua was old and stricken in years; and the LORD said unto him, Thou art old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed.

modern.text: Now Joshua was old and well along in years, and the LORD said to him, “You are old and well along in years, but very much of the land remains to be possessed.

original.text: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו אַתָּ֤ה זָקַ֨נְתָּה֙ בָּ֣אתָ בַיָּמִ֔ים וְהָאָ֛רֶץ נִשְׁאֲרָ֥ה הַרְבֵּֽה מְאֹ֖ד לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ

verses.restored: This is land remaining: all districts of Philistines and all Geshurites,

familiar.text: This is the land that yet remaineth: all the borders of the Philistines, and all Geshuri,

modern.text: This is the land that remains: All the territory of the Philistines and the Geshurites,

original.text: זֹ֥את הָאָ֖רֶץ הַנִּשְׁאָ֑רֶת כָּל גְּלִיל֥וֹת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וְכָל הַגְּשׁוּרִֽי

verses.restored: from Shihor which is before Egypt as far as border of Ekron northward, reckoned to Canaanite; five rulers of Philistines—the Gazite, Ashdodite, Ashkelonite, Gittite, and Ekronite—and Avvim,

familiar.text: From Sihor, which is before Egypt, even unto the borders of Ekron northward, which is counted to the Canaanite: five lords of the Philistines; the Gazathites, and the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avites:

modern.text: from the Shihor east of Egypt to the territory of Ekron on the north (considered to be Canaanite territory)—that of the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, as well as that of the Avvites;

original.text: מִֽן הַשִּׁיח֞וֹר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל פְּנֵ֣י מִצְרַ֗יִם וְעַ֨ד גְּב֤וּל עֶקְרוֹן֙ צָפ֔וֹנָה לַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י תֵּחָשֵׁ֑ב חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים הָעַזָּתִ֤י וְהָאַשְׁדּוֹדִי֙ הָאֶשְׁקְלוֹנִ֣י הַגִּתִּ֔י וְהָעֶקְרוֹנִ֖י וְהָעַוִּֽים

original.text: מִתֵּימָ֞ן כָּל אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֗י וּמְעָרָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַצִּידֹנִ֖ים עַד אֲפֵ֑קָה עַ֖ד גְּב֥וּל הָאֱמֹרִֽי

original.text: וְהָאָ֣רֶץ הַגִּבְלִ֗י וְכָל הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ מִזְרַ֣ח הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ מִבַּ֣עַל גָּ֔ד תַּ֖חַת הַר חֶרְמ֑וֹן עַ֖ד לְב֥וֹא חֲמָֽת

familiar.text: All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon unto Misrephothmaim, and all the Sidonians, them will I drive out from before the children of Israel: only divide thou it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee.

modern.text: All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim—all the Sidonians—I Myself will drive out before the Israelites. Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you.

original.text: כָּל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָ֠הָר מִֽן הַלְּבָנ֞וֹן עַד מִשְׂרְפֹ֥ת מַ֨יִם֙ כָּל צִ֣ידֹנִ֔ים אָֽנֹכִי֙ אוֹרִישֵׁ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל רַ֠ק הַפִּלֶ֤הָ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּֽנַחֲלָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוִּיתִֽיךָ

verses.restored: Now divide this land as inheritance to nine tribes and half tribe of Manasseh.

familiar.text: Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh,

modern.text: Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.” The Inheritance East of the Jordan (Numbers 32:1–42; Deuteronomy 3:12–22)

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה חַלֵּ֞ק אֶת הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את בְּנַחֲלָ֖ה לְתִשְׁעַ֣ת הַשְּׁבָטִ֑ים וַחֲצִ֖י הַשֵּׁ֥בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּֽׁה

verses.restored: With the other half, Reubenites and Gadites received their inheritance that Moses gave them across Jordan eastward, as Moses servant of YHWH gave them:

familiar.text: With whom the Reubenites and the Gadites have received their inheritance, which Moses gave them, beyond Jordan eastward, even as Moses the servant of the LORD gave them;

modern.text: The other half of Manasseh, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, had received the inheritance Moses had given them beyond the Jordan to the east, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had assigned to them:

original.text: עִמּ֗וֹ הָרֽאוּבֵנִי֙ וְהַגָּדִ֔י לָקְח֖וּ נַחֲלָתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר֩ נָתַ֨ן לָהֶ֜ם מֹשֶׁ֗ה בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ נָתַ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה

familiar.text: From Aroer, that is upon the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain of Medeba unto Dibon;

modern.text: The area from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the middle of the valley, the whole plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon,

original.text: מֵעֲרוֹעֵ֡ר אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל שְׂפַת נַ֨חַל אַרְנ֜וֹן וְהָעִ֨יר אֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּתוֹךְ הַנַּ֛חַל וְכָל הַמִּישֹׁ֥ר מֵידְבָ֖א עַד דִּיבֽוֹן

modern.text: and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;

original.text: וְכֹ֗ל עָרֵי֙ סִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלַ֖ךְ בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן עַד גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

familiar.text: All the kingdom of Og in Bashan, which reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei, who remained of the remnant of the giants: for these did Moses smite, and cast them out.

modern.text: the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who had reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei and had remained as a remnant of the Rephaim. Moses had struck them down and dispossessed them,

familiar.text: Nevertheless the children of Israel expelled not the Geshurites, nor the Maachathites: but the Geshurites and the Maachathites dwell among the Israelites until this day.

modern.text: but the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day.

original.text: וְלֹ֤א הוֹרִ֨ישׁוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת הַגְּשׁוּרִ֖י וְאֶת הַמַּעֲכָתִ֑י וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב גְּשׁ֤וּר וּמַֽעֲכָת֙ בְּקֶ֣רֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

familiar.text: Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the LORD God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance, as he said unto them.

modern.text: To the tribe of Levi, however, Moses had given no inheritance. The offerings made by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them. Reuben’s Inheritance

modern.text: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,

modern.text: all the cities of the plateau and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon until Moses killed him and the chiefs of Midian (Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba), the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.

modern.text: The Israelites also killed the diviner Balaam son of Beor along with the others they put to the sword.

modern.text: And the border of the Reubenites was the bank of the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the clans of the Reubenites, including the cities and villages. Gad’s Inheritance

translation_notes: Joshua's old age is acknowledged without contempt; the unfinished work is redistributed rather than making his worth depend on personal completion.
The chapter openly states that much land remains and names living Philistine, Geshurite, Sidonian, Canaanite, Gebalite, and other populations, complicating earlier claims of total conquest.
Philistine terminology and several geographic names may reflect later editorial horizons and require historical-linguistic audit.
Verse 6 promises future dispossession while ordering allotment before actual control, demonstrating that the map is aspirational as well as administrative.
Geshurites and Maacathites remain among Israel despite the dispossession ideal; the text's own social reality is more mixed than its conquest rhetoric.
Balaam is labeled diviner and briefly listed among the slain, requiring comparison with Numbers 22-31.
Levi's lack of territorial inheritance is framed as dependence upon YHWH and sanctuary offerings, which creates communal support obligations rather than clerical superiority.
The dense place list is ancient administrative geography, not a modern border instrument or permission to remove current inhabitants.
safety_note: Do not use Joshua 13 to justify modern territorial claims, displacement, ethnic mapping, contempt for aging leaders, or clerical privilege. Center honest acknowledgment of unfinished work, shared succession, the continued presence of diverse communities, and maps as historically situated texts rather than timeless deeds.
